subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration (function calling, streaming, embeddings/reranking)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration (function calling, streaming, embeddings/reranking)

Hi Ethan / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment. Please correct anything I've misunderstood.

Pain points you shared
- Current in-house embedding pipeline has inconsistent ranking quality and high infer-per-query cost at scale.
- Real-time features (live chat suggestions and re-ranking search results) are latency-sensitive (target P50 < 120ms).
- Need structured outputs (JSON with entity fields) for downstream analytics and transactionality with your CRM.

Goals
- Replace current batch embedding reranking with a hybrid approach: dense embeddings + light token-level reranking to improve MRR without large latency increases.
- Add streaming generation for chat assistants with function-calling hooks to run safe downstream actions.
- Deliver production-ready SDK integration with minimal changes to your backend.

What we proposed on the call
- Use Redwood streaming + function-calling for the chat path (low-latency partial responses, deterministic function outputs).
- Use embeddings + lightweight reranker for search; we recommend our 512-dense profile for your dataset and 8-bit quantization for scale.
- Structured-output schemas via function-calling or Redwood's structured-output option to produce JSON schema-validated results.

Open technical considerations
- SDK changes: small; primarily adding streaming client and a tiny function-call handler. Dev mentioned integrating our JS SDK in your microservice layer.
- KV/prefix caching for conversational flows to reduce token cost; we'd configure per-session policies.
- Security: you requested SOC 2 and details on data residency; we'll follow up with the security pack.

Next steps (owners + tentative dates)
- Redwood (Marissa): Send integration architecture + SOW draft (attached) — by EOD 3/15.
- Acme (Priya): Share sample schema and 2 example conversation logs (anonymized) — by 3/19.
- Redwood (Dev): Build a short SDK demo (streaming + function-calling) and a minimal reranking sample — by 3/22.
- Schedule technical working session with Priya + engineering — propose 30–45m for 3/23.

Attachments: redwood_integration_arch_overview.pdf (arch + recommended model profiles), SOW-draft-acme.docx (initial scope).

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@acme.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration (function calling, streaming, embeddings/reranking)

Thanks Marissa — solid recap and helpful to have the SOW up front. A couple of quick things from our side:

- Confirmed priorities: (1) Chat streaming + function-calling for our agent flows, (2) embeddings + reranking for search quality improvements. Latency target is important — we'll need a demo showing P50 numbers with the 512-d profile.
- Security ask: our InfoSec lead (cc: Priya) needs the SOC 2 report and a short memo on data retention + egress controls. Can you send those as part of the security pack?
- Budget/timing: We have an internal Q2 release window for search improvements. If Redwood can deliver an integration plan and demo by 3/22, we can evaluate for the sprint starting 4/5.

Yes to the proposed dates. For the working session on 3/23 — morning PST works for our team. Please send a calendar invite.

One more ask for the Dev demo: can the sample include a short example of structured output via function-calling (e.g., order extraction JSON) and an embeddings rerank snippet? That will help our engineers assess effort.

Ethan

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>, Ethan Rogers <ethan.rogers@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood demo repo + quick notes on SDK & structured outputs

Hi Priya / Ethan,

Following up with a short technical note ahead of the 3/23 session. I've created a tiny demo repo (we'll share link in the invite) with two examples:

1) Streaming + function-calling (Node.js)
- Uses Redwood JS SDK streaming client. Example shows partial responses and a deterministic function call that returns order-extraction JSON.
- Minimal server change: register a function handler and a small streaming consumer. We'll show patch diff (single-file change).

2) Embeddings + rerank (Python)
- We compute 512-d embeddings with our embeddings endpoint, then perform a lightweight reranker using a small cross-encoder run for top-10 candidates.
- Recommendation: use 8-bit quantized model for indexing nodes and the standard reranker model for top-k re-score to keep latency under 120ms for P50 (depends on your infra).

Structured output guidance
- Two paths: 1) function-calling (preferred for strict JSON outputs and schema validation) or 2) Redwood structured-output mode with a JSON schema to validate responses. We'll include both examples.

Please reply with a sample JSON schema you want validated (simple order schema or person extraction) and I'll wire it into the demo.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
